summary: Two suspicious iia values: area=2663 ha and production=2873.5 t are implausibly low; a third value of 2460450 t is implausibly high. The low values likely reflect a Chinese unit (thousand piculs/shi) mis-labeled as ha/tonnes in layer_b consolidation. The 2460450 t value is characteristic of 1930s iia data (IIA 1934-1938 averages: 2.32-2.71 Mt) and is either a temporally misassigned 1930s row or a unit-mismatch between an old iia pub (1000 quintals) and a newer pub (metric tonnes). Historical range for China groundnut production ca. 1909-1913 was likely 50k-200k t (Mitchell shows 404k t by 1922; iia export figures exceed 52k t in 1909-1913 average). Audit required: (1) trace raw source document for 2460450 t value; (2) verify unit column for 2873.5 t and 2663 ha in older iia pub; (3) flag both observations as unit-unverified and exclude from production aggregation until resolved. Polity CHN-1895-1913 itself is correct (CShapes 2.0 feature 710 vintage 1899). AUDIT DISCHARGED 2026-08-20. (2) THE UNIT HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED AND THE CAUSE IS MISATTRIBUTION. area=2663 and production=2873.5 are not Chinese figures in a mislabelled unit: they are JAPAN: KWANTUNG LEASED TERRITORY, period 1909-1913, from iia_1925_26, and the raw extract already carries them as `hectares` and `tonnes` -- so there is no thousand-piculs/shi conversion anywhere in the chain. Both values match the raw exactly and appear under no other raw label. 2,663 ha of groundnuts is unremarkable for the Liaodong leased territory; it is only absurd when read as all of China. Same class as issue 468: a value belonging to one label surfacing under another. Note the raw itself carries the identical pair twice -- period 1909-1913 in iia_1925_26 and period 1921-1925 in iia_1929_30 -- so the source repeated a stale figure across editions. (1) THE 2460450 t VALUE NO LONGER EXISTS. No layer-B groundnut row is within 1% of it, and it appears nowhere in the raw extract; layer B has been rebuilt since this entry was logged on 2026-06-29. The entry's instinct was right, though: the 1930s china series is real and the volume disagreement behind it is already tracked in edition_conflicts.csv -- `china, groundnut, production, 1933: iia_1933_34 191,860 vs iia_1938_39 2,980,600, ratio 15.54, classed revised`. So the 'temporally misassigned 1930s row' reading was the correct family; the specific value is gone. (3) The requested flag is therefore unnecessary for the 2460450 row and should apply to the two Kwantung cells only, and as a REROUTE rather than a unit correction. SEPARATE OBSERVATION, NOT PART OF THIS ENTRY: mitchell's china groundnut production for 1931-1934 equals raw iia's for 1933-1936 to mitchell's 1-kt rounding (2,981,000/2,980,600; 2,644,000/2,644,400; 2,249,000/2,248,600; 2,631,000/2,631,100) while the same two sources agree at the SAME year in 1922-1924 and 1943-1944, so one of them misdates that four-year block by two years. Which one is not determined here -- the levels are plausible either way -- and it needs its own entry. MECHANISM ESTABLISHED 2026-08-21, and it is broader than this entry's 'a value belonging to one label surfacing under another'. Layer B's iia `china, mainland` cell is the ARITHMETIC SUM of raw `china` and raw `japan: kwantung leased territory`, exact to the digit in 23 of the 24 groundnut cells and across the whole label in 46 of 48 comparable cells. Where china has no figure the sum degenerates to Kwantung alone -- which is the case this audit found, and the case issue 483 counts, 25 uniquely-attributable cells. Where china DOES have a figure, Kwantung is ADDED to it: 21 further cells, a disjoint population that no attribution-by-value test can see, because the published number equals neither component. By item: groundnuts 8 cells (inflation 1.0255-1.2724), soybeans 8 (1.0030-1.0110), sesame seed 5 (1.0001-1.0016). Soybeans is an item 483 never associates with Kwantung at all -- it appears there only as a `china: manchuria` contributor -- precisely because every one of its Kwantung cells is additive. Measuring the identity independently also reproduces 483's 25 exactly, by different means, which corroborates it. ONE CELL IS NEITHER: groundnut area at 1933 publishes 34,600, which is Kwantung's figure from iia_1925_26-era numbering in iia_1933_34, while iia_1938_39 prints Kwantung 35,000 AND china 1,542,000 -- so the cell is not a sum and not a same-volume replacement, and the real China figure is dropped. Remedy still blocked on 400 (Kwantung has no destination polity). Also verified: the two low values are carried in the raw as `hectares` and `tonnes`, so the thousand-piculs hypothesis has no conversion to point at anywhere in the chain.

summary: Confirmed data ingestion error in data/external/before_1961.csv for China mainland goats sourced from mitchell/page251-300.xlsx sheet page_41_table_1. Root cause: the import script applied a wrong unit multiplier to the raw Excel values (which are in thousands, unit column B=1000), yielding values ~1001x too large for 1950-1960 and ~2x too large for 1945-1947. Specifically: the reviewed Excel has raw values like 1821 (1950) in column J; these should be multiplied by 1000 to get heads (1821000 goats in 1950), but stored values are e.g. 1822821000 = 1821 * 1001 * 1000. For 1945-1947 the Excel goats values (13249 13609 13976) are stored as 26498000 / 27218000 / 27952000 = exactly 2000x each raw value instead of 1000x. The 1949 cell J7 is a text annotation '16130 millions'; the import parsed the numeric part 16130 and stored 16146130 which is only 0.1% above the correct ~16130000 and is plausible. No territorial or polity-boundary action needed. Action required: fix the import pipeline to apply unit multiplier x1000 only (not x1001000) for China mainland goats rows from page_41_table_1 then regenerate before_1961.csv and re-run the flag pipeline. The corrected 1950 value should be 1821000 heads (not 1.82 billion); 1950-1960 series should all be divided by 1001; 1945-1947 series should be divided by 2. Source file: /home/usuario/Nextcloud/WHEP_ERC 2025/Sources/data_raw/sources_reviewed/mitchell/Agriculture without Europe data/page251-300.xlsx sheet page_41_table_1 column J (Goats). RE-TESTED 2026-08-24. Every figure reproduces, and the mechanism is provable by DIVISIBILITY: all eleven values for 1950-1960 divide by 1001 into a whole thousand (1,822,821,000/1001 = 1,821,000; 5,122,117,000/1001 = 5,117,000), and 1945-1947 divide by 2000 into the raw Excel integers 13249 / 13609 / 13976 exactly. Eleven exact divisions is not a coincidence any alternative explanation survives. ONE CORRECTION TO THE REMEDY: this entry calls 1949 'only 0.1% above the correct ~16130000 and is plausible', which reads as a cell needing no repair. It is not a separate benign case -- 16,146,130 is EXACTLY 16,130 x 1001, i.e. the IDENTICAL wrong multiplier with the x1000 unit factor missing, because the source cell is the text annotation '16130 millions' so the unit multiplier never applied. 1949 is in fact the cleanest demonstration of the mechanism: with the unit factor absent, 1001-instead-of-1000 shows up as precisely 0.1%. The correct value is therefore derivable (16,130,000) and the remedy should cover 1949 rather than leave it. NOTE ON RE-TESTABILITY: data/external/before_1961.csv is gitignored and machine-local, so this entry's re-test SKIPS with a named report where the file is absent rather than passing silently.

summary: iia magnitudes in layer B are not on a common scale, so the magnitude_continuity check of assertion verification is UNUSABLE for iia assertions (27 of the 158 assertions the legacy bare-label tier was hiding, including the tier's largest, serbia|iia|1920-1944 at 573 rows). Measured on consolidated_layer_b.parquet (26,175 iia rows, 164 labels, 1909-1945), median wheat production in 'tonnes': canada 756,867; denmark 690,589; sweden 497,275; germany 293,228; france 101,145; united kingdom 96,525; serbia 14,618; netherlands 1,103. Denmark and Sweden are plausible for the interwar period; France (~8 Mt), Germany (~4-5 Mt), Canada (~10-14 Mt) and the Netherlands (~150 kt) are one to two orders of magnitude low, so the error is per-table, not a single global factor that could be divided out. Area is affected too: median wheat area in 'ha' 1930-1938 is russian federation 125,800, serbia 58,000, czech republic 5,000 - the USSR/Serbia ratio is 2.2 where the real one is ~90. Within one series the scale also flips: serbia wheat area is 58,000 ha for 1934 and 17,000 ha for the 1934-1938 average. Audit required: trace the unit column and any multiplier applied per iia publication/table during layer_b consolidation. Until then, iia assertions must be verified on scope/vintage/documentary grounds only and a verifier must not read iia staple_magnitudes as evidence of reporting scope. No polity or territorial action follows from this row. AUDIT DISCHARGED 2026-08-20, AND EVERY LEG OF THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE IS REFUTED. The entry asked to 'trace the unit column and any multiplier applied per iia publication/table during layer_b consolidation'. Done: of all 12,052 layer-B iia `tonnes` rows, 10,810 (89.7%) carry a value that appears VERBATIM among the raw extract's production values for the same year, and only 112 (0.9%) need a power-of-ten factor to find a raw match -- x10 29, x100 49, x1000 34, which is the size of the already-confirmed iia-tobacco-implausible-magnitudes / iia-hops-x100 / iia-1933-x10-wrong-volume-cells classes rather than a new one. A per-table rescaling during consolidation would produce a LOW verbatim rate; 90% is incompatible with it. THE MAGNITUDE EVIDENCE WAS A WRONG-ITEM COMPARISON. Both legs cited `wheat`, and iia-wheat-is-spelt-and-meslin (confirmed, logged later) establishes that the iia `wheat` item is spelt and meslin -- the raw extract carries ZERO wheat production rows. Against raw spelt+meslin the layer-B medians are the SAME series, not one to two orders low: canada 756,867 vs 771,015; denmark 690,589 vs 745,022; sweden 497,275 vs 502,537; france 101,145 vs 97,650; uk 96,525 vs 87,906 (uk: england and wales). Those are plausible magnitudes for the crop they actually are -- Danish and Swedish blandsaed, French meteil, Canadian mixed grain -- and the Netherlands' 1,103 t, flagged here as absurd for wheat, is unremarkable for a minor mixed grain. THE AREA RATIO IS CORRECT IN LAYER B. This entry reads the USSR/Serbia area ratio as 2.2 'where the real one is ~90'; ~90 is a WHEAT ratio. For spelt+meslin the comparable raw quantity is the per-year SUM of the two products, and its medians give ussr 157,150 ha against yugoslavia 79,000 ha, a ratio of 1.99 -- so layer-B's 2.2 is right. (A first pass at this refutation reported 4.44 by taking the median of individual product ROWS instead of per-year sums, which is the same wrong-aggregate mistake in miniature.) CONSEQUENCE: the blocker on iia magnitude verification is ITEM IDENTITY, not scale, and it is documented by iia-wheat-is-spelt-and-meslin and iia-item-series-switch-raw-products. The instruction above -- that iia assertions be verified on scope/vintage/documentary grounds only -- rests on refuted grounds and costs the 27 assertions this entry names, including its largest, serbia|iia|1920-1944 at 573 rows. STATUS LEFT AT pending_audit DELIBERATELY: refuting the evidence offered is not the same as proving iia magnitudes ARE on a common scale, which should rest on a positive test, and lifting a verifier instruction is a curation call. POSITIVE TEST NOW MECHANICAL, 2026-08-21. The paragraph above leaves this entry at pending_audit because 'refuting the evidence offered is not the same as proving iia magnitudes ARE on a common scale, which should rest on a positive test'. That test is now run by 35_retest_data_errors.py on every pass, and it reproduces the figures quoted above exactly: of 12,052 dated layer-B iia `tonnes` rows, 10,810 (89.7%) carry a value appearing VERBATIM among the raw extract's production figures for the same year and 112 (0.9%) need a power of ten (/100 59, /10 36, x10 9, /1000 4, x100 3, x1000 1). The logic is that a per-publication or per-table multiplier applied during consolidation -- the mechanism this entry asked to be traced -- would make the verbatim rate LOW, so 89.7% is incompatible with it. THE TEST'S OWN WEAKNESS IS STATED IN ITS DOCSTRING: matching against every raw production value for the same year does not check that the value came from the right label or product, and a round number will find a partner. That is acceptable here because the claim under test is about SCALE, which a rescaled panel would fail however the labels line up; per-cell provenance is the strict join in cell_attribution.csv instead. STATUS STILL LEFT AT pending_audit: lifting the verifier instruction is a curation call, but it now rests on a checked figure rather than on prose, and a regression in the verbatim rate would fail the re-test rather than passing unnoticed.

label: (nested reporting levels; see summary)
summary: A polity can receive TWO OR MORE NESTING LEVELS of the same territory from the SAME source, so any aggregation over polity_code either sums a whole with its own parts or reads a cell that holds two incompatible values. Measured 2026-08-17 by routing all 189,839 matched layer-B rows through the assertion segments and grouping on (polity_code, source, item, indicator, year, unit): 52 such cells hold 110 rows contributed by more than one source label, and NONE of the colliding values are equal, so this is not duplicate ingestion but genuinely different series landing on one key. Worst cases: PNG-1949-1975 [fao1952] 18 rows from 'papua' + 'new guinea' (the two component territories FAO still reported separately after the 1949 union); CHN-1949-1950 13 rows and CHN-1947-1949 12 rows from 'china' + 'china 22 provinces' + 'china manchuria' (the 22-provinces rows are China proper EXCLUDING Manchuria: their land-use totals are 507,182 vs 106,930 thousand ha, i.e. ~5.07M km2 vs ~1.07M km2, so the two are disjoint components of the polity); FID-1887-1954 10 rows from 'indochina' + 'indochina viet nam'; KOR-1948-2025 10 rows from 'korea' + 'korea south'; DEU-1920-1938 9 rows from 'germany' + 'germany western' + 'germany berlin' for 1937 alone, which leaves the Reich polity carrying three mutually incompatible 1937 population values (Berlin's 4,284 thousand among them, against a Reich total near 67 million); JPN-1895-1945 [iia] 8 rows from 'japan' + 'palau'; GBR-1921-2025 8 rows from 'united kingdom' + 'united kingdom great britain' (Great Britain excludes Northern Ireland); CHN-1950-2025 6 rows; SER-1878-1913 [juan] 4 rows from 'serbia' + 'yugoslav sfr'; and 2 rows each on ETH-1907-1936/ETH-1936-1941/ETH-1941-1952 ('ethiopia' + 'ethiopia pdr'), PAL-1920-1948 ('israel' + 'palestine'), VGB-1800-2025 and ZAF-1910-2025 ('south africa' + 'natal'). Aggregate-level nesting without cell conflicts exists too and is not counted here (BWI-1833-1962 and BLI-1833-1960 beside their constituent islands; GCT-1919-1956 beside GHA-1898-1957 and BTL-1920-1957; PYF-1800-2025 beside 'makatea'; USA-1867-1959 beside 'alaska'/'guam'/'american samoa'/'virgin islands us'). This is the same hazard already recorded for one label in united-states-california-double-count, generalised and quantified. Audit required: decide, per family, which nesting level the polity represents, then either drop the other level (as the California row does) or give the component its own polity/segment. Fourteen legacy-tier assertions were quarantined rather than confirmed on this ground (see quarantine.csv, 2026-08-17); each names the missing segment where one exists: MAN-1945-1950 already covers 1945-1949 Manchuria, TNGU-1920-1949 and TPAP-1906-1949 end at the 1949 PNG union, BRL-1938-1945 and WZO-1938-1949 both start in 1938 so the 1937 Berlin and western-zone rows have no target, and the Caroline Islands have no polity for the 1914-1920 Japanese occupation (GCAR-1899-1914 -> CAR-1920-1945). No polity or polygon change is made here. WHAT THE AUDIT ACTUALLY REQUIRES, MEASURED 2026-08-20: for each family, does a polity exist whose TERRITORY is the component and whose span covers the conflicting years? Only ONE of ten does. CHN-1947-1949 and CHN-1949-1950 can send their `china manchuria` rows to MAN-1945-1950 (1947-1949 covered); CHN-1950-2025's 1950-1951 manchuria rows cannot, because that row ends exactly at 1950. Every other family needs a polity that does not exist: PNG-1949-1975's papua+new guinea rows are 1950-1951 while TPAP-1906-1949 and TNGU-1920-1949 both end at the union; DEU-1920-1938's berlin and western-zone rows are 1937 while BRL, WZO and SBZ all start in 1938 -- but THIS ONE NEEDS NO POLITY, corrected 2026-08-20: there was no West Germany or Allied-sector Berlin in 1937, so a 1937 row for either would assert an entity that did not exist. FAO computed the 1937 figures for the territories that LATER became those units -- `Germany Western` population 38,510 thousand and `Germany Berlin` 4,284 thousand, both correct for what they describe against a Reich total near 67 million -- which is the post-war-unit back-projection class of issue 450, not a missing row. The labels carry the `1934-1938` period alongside the dated 1937 (77 of the Berlin/Western/Eastern rows have a period), so part of the population never reaches the R package while the dated 1937 rows do. The three colliding values are not three opinions about one quantity but three different territories, so the consumer's mean over the duplicate key describes nothing -- which is the harm, and it is fixed by issue 450's convention (route to the polity that existed at the data year and mark the basis, or drop) rather than by creating a row. That leaves five families needing a polity, not eight -- see the SER and KOR corrections below; JPN-1895-1945's palau rows are 1915-1918, in the gap between GCAR-1899-1914 and CAR-1920-1945; KOR-1948-2025 receives `korea` meaning the PENINSULA for 1949-1951, for which no polity exists after KOR-1945-1948 (and the peninsula is NOT PRK); ZAF-1910-2025 receives `natal` after NAT-1895-1910 ends; GBR-1921-2025 receives Great Britain exclusive of Northern Ireland, which has no row; SER-1878-1913 receives `yugoslav sfr` decades before any Yugoslav polity -- and THIS ONE NEEDS NO POLITY EITHER, corrected 2026-08-20, on the same ground as the German case: creating a Yugoslav row for 1909-1911 would assert a state that did not exist until 1918, so it is issue 450's back-projection class. The 11 rows are hemp/hempseed 15,000-15,700 ha, potatoes 10,400-12,400 and flax/linseed 1,800 against juan `serbia`'s 6,940-7,650, 11,000-44,050 and 380-1,700 for the same years. NOT CLAIMED: which territory those rows describe. They are not Yugoslavia-scale -- Serbia was about 48,000 km2 against the federation's 248,000, so a whole-federation figure should run several times Serbia's, and hemp is 2x while potatoes is sometimes LESS. That is consistent with the label covering the future federation MINUS Serbia (the Habsburg lands, reported separately at the time) but two labels being present and different only proves they are not the same series; magnitude cannot name a territory. KOR-1948-2025 IS ALSO NOT A CREATION CASE: issue 355 established that `korea` there means the PENINSULA, which decomposes into KOR-1948-2025 and PRK-1948-2025, both existing -- so it is a whole-beside-parts question (drop, flag is_aggregate, or reattribute by subtraction), not a missing row. NET: of ten families, ONE is a mechanical reroute (china manchuria 1947-1949 -> MAN-1945-1950), THREE need a convention scoped elsewhere (DEU and SER to issue 450, KOR to aggregate handling), and FIVE are genuinely issue 400: PNG papua+new guinea 1950-1951, CHN-1950-2025 manchuria 1950-1951, JPN palau 1915-1918, ZAF natal, GBR Great Britain exclusive of Northern Ireland. The reduction from ten came entirely from asking whether the missing entity ever existed, which a span check cannot ask. THE FIVE ARE NOT HOMOGENEOUS, graded 2026-08-20 by whether the component had an administration -- which is precisely what issue 400 asks about: `natal` (mitchell, 40 of its 422 rows land on ZAF-1910-2025 while 305 route to NAT-1843-1895 and 110 to NAT-1895-1910) was a PROVINCE of South Africa, so this one is not a creation case at all but an extension of the existing NAT family past the 1910 Union, the smallest ask of the five and with precedent in the rows already there; `papua` + `new guinea` (fao1952, 22 of 34) were legally distinct territories under a joint administration from 1949; `china manchuria` (fao1952, 7 of 36) was administered by the Northeast People's Government 1949-1954; `palau` (iia, 4 of 14) was under the Japanese naval administration of the South Seas 1914-1922. All four had their own officials and records. `united kingdom great britain` (fao1952, 3 of 9) is the ONLY purely statistical grouping -- England, Scotland and Wales have no administration distinct from the UK's, so it is a line the compiler drew inside a state that governs the whole of it, and the weakest of the five under any reading of issue 400. Counting correction: `natal` was first reported here as having zero rows, from searching fao1952 and iia when the label is mitchell's. So the audit is not ten independent judgements -- for eight families the judgement is already implied by this entry's own framing and what is missing is the ROW, which makes those eight instances of issue 400 rather than of this audit. IT IS ALSO THE BOTTLENECK FOR THE QUARANTINE: 13 of the 34 quarantine rows with no review verdict scope-match this entry (china manchuria x3, china 22 provinces x3, germany berlin, germany western, palau, yugoslav sfr, united kingdom great britain, new guinea, papua), so a reviewer asked to adjudicate one of them is being asked this audit's question one cell at a time. Resolving this entry is therefore higher-leverage than working that queue. METHOD WARNING: a span-only test gives the wrong answer. Asking merely whether some polity sharing a code prefix covers the years returns 5 of 10, because PRK-1948-2025 covers 1949-1951 (but North Korea is not the peninsula), GBM-1895-1946 covers 1937 (but GBM is British MALAYA), and SER-1816-1913 covers 1909-1911 (but it is the same family, not a Yugoslav row). The territory has to be read, not inferred from the code. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-21, AND BOTH HALVES OF THE 2026-08-17 STATEMENT HAVE MOVED. Cells with more than one source label: 72, not 52; rows in them: 173, not 110 -- a 38% drift, consistent with matched_rows growing from 189,839 to 190,529 rows. MORE IMPORTANTLY THE DIAGNOSIS IS FALSIFIED IN PART: the entry states that 'NONE of the colliding values are equal, so this is not duplicate ingestion but genuinely different series landing on one key', and 7 cells now have two DIFFERENT labels sharing a value -- ETH-1907-1936, ETH-1936-1941 and ETH-1941-1952 coffee green, where `ethiopia` and `ethiopia pdr` are equal (19,800 / 16,300 / 17,000 t); KOR-1948-2025 commercial nitrogenous fertilizers at 1950, 1951 and 1951, where `Korea` and `Korea South` are equal (14.6 / 48.2 / 0.03); and PNG-1949-1975 crawler tractors 1950, where `New Guinea` and `Papua` both read 8. SIX OF THE SEVEN ARE EXPLAINED BY LATER WORK IN THIS REPO: `ethiopia`/`ethiopia pdr` is a pure duplicate (issue 451; label_hierarchy_identity.csv classes it `duplicate` at 3 of 3 cells exact), and the Korea cells are years where the peninsula total equals the South because the North was not reported (issues 451, 521 -- at 1949 the same series reads Korea 108.9 = Korea South 98.9 + Korea North 10.0). The seventh, two labels both reading 8, is what coincidence looks like. So the entry's SCOPE claim stands but its MECHANISM claim is now mixed: most colliding cells are genuinely different series, and at least 6 are duplicate ingestion. Re-tested mechanically from 2026-08-21 (35_retest_data_errors.py); the equality count is the load-bearing figure, because a drifting cell count means the panel moved while a rising equality count means the diagnosis is wrong.

summary: iia `hops` (tonnes) is carried 100x too large over 1934-1945, on the same evidence and in the same window as iia-tobacco-implausible-magnitudes -- and this commodity was NOT previously recorded. Examples: F248 1935 iia 189,100 vs juan 1,891; 1937 iia 213,200 vs juan 2,132; F51 1934 iia 707,400 vs juan 7,074. World hop production in this period was on the order of 100,000 t, so 189,100 t for Yugoslavia alone is impossible on its own terms. That tobacco and hops share one factor, one window and one set of polities suggests a single extraction or unit fault affecting a group of items rather than a per-commodity error, so OTHER iia items in 1934-1945 should be checked the same way wherever a cross-source comparison exists. Two further cells sit at 13.3x and 98.5x rather than exactly 100x and are NOT explained by this. Repair for a compared cell is division by 100; for hops cells with no cross-source comparison the factor is inferred rather than measured. HOPS ALSO CARRIES A SEPARATE x10 ON ITS AREA, MEASURED 2026-08-20, and this entry's remedy is incomplete without it. Same-year 1933 pairs where iia_1933_34 and iia_1938_39 both report: hops PRODUCTION n=15, median factor 100.00x, 15 of 15 within 20% of 100x; hops AREA n=16, median 10.04x, 14 of 16 within 20% of 10x. For contrast tobacco AREA is CLEAN -- n=46, median 1.00x, 32 of 46 within 5% of 1x -- and across EVERY item zero area pairs fall in the 30-300x band, so the x100 is production-only and the hops area x10 is a second, distinct defect. THE LATE VOLUME ALSO ROUNDS IT: every late hops-area value is a multiple of 1,000 (hungary 107 -> 1,000; france 1,708 -> 17,000; uk 6,837 -> 68,000; usa 12,262 -> 123,000) against precise clean values, so the unit is ten times smaller AND rounded to the nearest 1,000 of it, i.e. the nearest 100 ha. That explains the only two apparent outliers: austria (56 ha -> 1,000) and romania (2 ha -> 1,000) sit BELOW the rounding floor, so their factors of 17.9x and 500x are the floor rather than a third defect -- the same grid-resolution phenomenon gated by validate_grid_ambiguous_zeros.py. THIS RECONCILES THE YIELD FIGURES: issue 433 records tobacco breaking at 70x and hops at 21x on implied yield with no explanation. Yield is production over area, so tobacco inflates 100/1 and hops 100/10 = 10. The items differ on yield BECAUSE hops' area is inflated too, which also means a yield-based screen understates hops tenfold and is likely why yield_series_corrections.csv reaches so few hops series. EXPOSURE IN THE PANEL, STATED AS AN INFERENCE: 38-41 layer-B hops area rows fall at 1934+, i.e. in the window where the defect was measured at its 1933 boundary. That the x10 CONTINUES past 1933 is an inference rather than a measurement -- same volume, same column, no reason to change mid-run -- because after 1933 there is no clean volume to compare against. Two weaker arguments were tried and both fail: the panel's hops-area median rising from 271 to 4,000 ha is confounded by composition, since different countries report in each period; and the on-a-1000-grid share is NOT a defect signature at all -- 96% of ALL 3,393 iia area rows at 1934+ sit on that grid, across 27 items with a median jump of 91 percentage points, which is the reporting grid already recorded for these volumes (see the iia grid convention and issue 446). Hops is BELOW the field at 50% on-grid, so the grid says nothing in its favour either way. REMEDY: hops production /100 AND hops area /10, with values under about 100 ha unrecoverable because the source rounded them to its floor. Dividing hops production alone would leave its area ten times high and its yield ten times low, which is worse than leaving both because it would look repaired. See issue #416.

summary: A layer-B iia ITEM SERIES can be stitched from several DIFFERENT raw products, switching year to year, so its level shifts are product switches rather than changes in output. 28 series mix raw products whose levels differ by >=3x, each product supplying >=2 cells. The switches go BACK AND FORTH, which is what rules out growth as the explanation. CLEAREST CASE, australia / sugar raw centrifugal / tonnes, 33 cells: cane 131,961 t (1912) -> BEET 922 (1913, x0.01) -> beet through 1919 -> cane 165,616 (1920, x105) -> cane 297,700 (1921) -> BEET 2,829 (1922, x0.01) -> `sugar: cane, unrefined` 537,212 (1925, x175) -> cane through 1938 (783,200) -> BEET 6,400 (1939, x0.01) -> cane 611,300 (1944, x873). Australia's beet sugar industry was negligible, so 12 of the 33 cells are about 1/300 of the series they sit in. OTHERS: sweden p (superphosphate -> basic slag x0.08 -> superphosphate x28); japan n (calcium cyanamide with ammonium sulfate in 1919 x27 and 1933 x5); japan p x26; norway p x17; congo and niger cotton lint (cotton vs cotton: ginned, 8-11x); czech republic grapes (grapes: table vs vineyards: all vs grapes: wine vs vineyards: grapes+raisins -- five products in a 17-value series, 8 ha against 27,000 ha); australia/cyprus/japan/israel/turkey grapes; usa and australia raisins. WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: the source never changes, so 16_source_splices.py sees no seam; the values are plausible for the product they came from, so no magnitude screen fires; and the item name is constant, so nothing keyed on it notices. CONSEQUENCE: any trend, growth rate or level-shift reading of an affected series is measuring the yearbook's choice of table, not agriculture. This is the mechanism behind part of issue #360's level-shift confound. NOT REPAIRABLE by rescaling -- each cell needs re-attributing to its own item. See issue #378. USA SUGAR IS THE MOST SEVERE INSTANCE AND ALSO SWITCHES TERRITORIAL SCOPE, not just product. `united states of america / sugar raw centrifugal / tonnes`, 33 dated cells, has FOUR regimes and NONE of them is a national total, each verified by exact subset-sum against the raw extract: 1909-1921 `usa`/BEET ONLY (39-81% of that year's US sugar, all cane missing); 1922-1925 `usa: louisiana and florida`/cane unrefined (4-19%); 1930-1938 CANE ONLY summed over `usa` + `us puerto rico` + `usa: hawaii`, beet excluded (77-90%) -- 1930 = 166,643.5 + 710,473.7 + 896,854.0 = 1,773,971.2 and 1938 = 491,800 + 827,000 + 835,000 = 2,153,800; 1939-1945 `usa: louisiana and florida`/cane (10-21%). So the scope oscillates between one state pair, the mainland's beet crop, and a three-territory cane aggregate. `puerto rico` routes to `united states of america` (kind=shares_target) and the raw carries its sugar continuously from 314,599 t in 1909 to 985,000 t in 1941, but it is inside the published figure ONLY for 1930-1938 -- included in 9 years of 33 and absent in the other 24. NOT double-counted: there are zero layer-B sugar rows under any Puerto Rico label, so the hypothesis was tested and refuted. Issue #443's account of this series is retracted in its own comments: its '1938 carries both 2,153,800 and 361,500' was a `1934-1938` PERIOD row read as a dated year, so there is no same-year duplicate and no interleaving at a point, and its '1909-1921 national scale' is beet only. See issues #443, #490. RE-TESTED MECHANICALLY 2026-08-21, AND THE AUSTRALIA EXHIBIT CARRIES TWO MECHANISMS, NOT ONE. Matching every cell of layer-B australia / sugar raw centrifugal / tonnes against the raw extract's own (label, product, year, value): 37 cells, of which 19 are australia / `sugar: cane` (the real series), 17 are australia / `sugar: beet` (the defect, about 1/300 of the series) and ONE is not a product switch at all. So the cane/beet alternation is real and is this entry's subject, while the 1925 cell is label contamination and belongs with issues 372 and 483. COUNTS CORRECTED: this entry says '33 cells' with '12 of the 33' on the wrong product; the series now has 37 cells with 17 on beet, so the defect is larger than recorded and the re-test pins the measured figures rather than the quoted ones.

label: (12+ labels incl. argentina, australia, belgium, chile, egypt, japan)
summary: The layer-B iia item `flax fibre and tow` is MAJORITY LINSEED -- the seed, not the fibre -- even though a separate `linseed` item exists (377 rows). Flax gives two products from one plant and they are not interchangeable: linseed is an oilseed, flax fibre and tow is a textile fibre, and the quantities differ by orders of magnitude for the same country. Measured against the raw IIA extract with the raw label required to match the layer-B label: of 543 `flax fibre and tow` cells, 168 match raw `linseed` and 109 match raw `flax: fibre`; 58 match BOTH and are ambiguous. So 110 cells are unambiguously LINSEED against 51 unambiguously flax fibre -- the item carries more of the crop it is not named for. 19 OF THOSE CELLS ARE ALSO PRESENT UNDER THE LAYER-B `linseed` ITEM at the same label, year, value and unit, so one observation is counted twice and any oilseed or fibre aggregate summing both items double-counts them. Magnitude check that makes the direction obvious: argentina appears with 1,590,000 t (1933), 2,025,000 t (1934) and 2,059,000 ha (1935) under `flax fibre and tow`. Argentina was the world's largest LINSEED producer and grew essentially no flax fibre; world flax fibre output was on the order of 500,000 t in total, so these are linseed figures. Also affected: australia, belgium, bolivia, chile, egypt, japan, mexico, new zealand, sweden, turkey, uruguay. NOT REPAIRABLE BY RESCALING: each cell needs re-attributing to the correct item, and the 58 ambiguous cells cannot be attributed from the panel at all. HYPOTHESIS, NOT MEASURED: issue #360's worst source splice is `united states / flax fibre and tow / ha` at x1655 across a juan->mitchell boundary, and a linseed-vs-fibre switch would produce exactly that. I cannot test it, because the raw extract I have is IIA's and that splice is between two other sources. See issue #380. RE-TESTED 2026-08-21, AND THE COUNTS ARE JOIN-SENSITIVE. The POPULATION reproduces exactly -- 543 cells, being dated rows whose layer-B label has a provenance mapping -- so that half of the method is recoverable and confirmed. The match counts are not. Joining through `dominant_raw_label`, the extract's OWN label and the correct join per iia_label_provenance.csv's own note, gives 209 cells matching raw `linseed` alone against 107 matching raw `flax: fibre` alone and 88 ambiguous. Joining through the CANONICAL `raw_label` instead gives 137 / 57 / 50. The figures recorded above (110 / 51 / 58) are reproducible by NEITHER join and sit closest to the canonical one -- which matches the extract in only 32% of rows, so a count built on it understates any label-matched total, exactly the direction these figures sit in. THE CONCLUSION IS UNAFFECTED AND IS STRENGTHENED: linseed leads flax fibre by roughly 2:1 under either join (209:107 or 137:57), so the item is majority linseed either way, and on the defensible join the defect is about 90% larger than recorded. The re-test pins the dominant-label figures and names its join in its docstring rather than restating numbers whose derivation cannot be recovered.

label: France Germany; France Eastern; Western; Eastern
summary: PROVEN BY ARITHMETIC: in fao1952's hemp-fibre table the labels `France Germany`, `France Eastern` and `Western` are GERMANY, GERMANY EASTERN and GERMANY WESTERN. The yearbook page listed France, then Germany with indented Eastern/Western sub-rows, and the extraction carried the preceding country name forward onto the sub-rows -- inconsistently, since `Western` kept no prefix. The proof is internal and needs no source page: `France Eastern` + `Western` = `France Germany` EXACTLY on both indicators for 1934-1938 -- production 2.9 + 1.2 = 4.1 (1000 t) and area 4.0 + 2.0 = 6.0 (1000 ha) -- which is the parent/child identity, and the table contains NO bare `Germany` label at all while carrying `France` separately at 3.9. A France-plus-Germany aggregate would not equal the sum of two German zones, and France's own row would not also be present. AFFECTED: 6 rows (2 per label). Small, but it is the only instance of this defect anywhere in the panel that can be settled from the numbers alone, so it is the template for the rest. WHAT THIS IS NOT: fao1952 encodes hierarchy by CONCATENATING parent and child, and that is normal and correct. `Germany Western` (254 rows), `China Taiwan` (143), `Korea South` (131), `Indochina Viet Nam` (109), `British Borneo Sarawak` (44) and `Libya Tripolitania` (37) are real parent-child labels; 46 labels share the surface pattern and 1,512 of their 1,567 rows are correctly assigned. The defect is only where the prefix is NOT a parent of the remainder -- `France Germany`, `Australia Fiji`, `Leeward Islands Trinidad and Tobago`, `Union of South Africa Zanzibar & Pemba` -- which takes geographic knowledge to tell apart and cannot be detected from the label shape. About 55 rows in total. See issue #29. WIDENED 2026-08-20: the bare label `Eastern` belongs here too, and the identity now holds for 18 rows rather than 6, by the same sum-identity method. The entry proved `France Eastern` + `Western` = `France Germany` in the hemp-fibre table. The same structure appears in TWO further tables, where the parent `Germany` is present under its own name and the residual is a CONSTANT third term: agricultural population 1937 W 10,091 + E 3,037 = 13,128 against Germany 13,145, and 1951 W 8,096 + E 3,488 = 11,584 against 11,601 -- residual exactly 17 BOTH years; goats 1949 W 1,428 + E 1,398 = 2,826 against 2,831, 1950 3,089 against 3,094, 1951 2,957 against 2,962 -- residual exactly 5 ALL THREE years. A residual that is constant across years is a third term, not noise, and Berlin is the only German unit unaccounted for in either table; `Germany  Berlin` does appear in the population table with agricultural sub-rows (32 occupied, 17 female, 15 male for 1951). CZECHOSLOVAKIA IS EXCLUDED: its agricultural population is 4,621 (1937) and 3,396 (1951) and its goats 982, none of which is close. That mattered because the magnitudes invite it -- `Western`'s 10,091 falling to 8,096 looks like the Czech lands losing the Sudeten German population, and it is only wrong because `Western` carries the AGRICULTURAL indicator while the Czech comparison figure is TOTAL population. ROW ACCOUNTING: `Western` has 13 layer-B rows and `Eastern` 5, all 18 UNROUTED (whep_code null). Of them, 7 are now settled arithmetically (2 hemp 1934-38 by the original proof, 2 population and 3 goats by the residuals above); 6 more are hemp 1949-1951 under `Western` alone, where no parent or sibling exists in those years, so they rest on continuity within a table whose label identity is proven; and the remaining period rows cannot reach published output either way (issue 310). The sibling labels already route -- `germany western` 254 rows to F78-1949-1990/DEU-1920-1938/WZO-1938-1949 and `germany eastern` 109 rows to F77-1949-1990/SBZ-1938-1949 -- so unlike issues 422 and 483 a destination exists, and 14 of the 18 rows (the 1949-1951 ones) are a mechanical reroute rather than a decision. The 2 rows dated 1937 land in issue 411's open question about post-war zones measured on 1937 territory. No alias changed. RE-TESTED MECHANICALLY 2026-08-21 (35_retest_data_errors.py), AND THE ROW COUNT ABOVE IS AN UNDERCOUNT. The identity reproduces exactly on both indicators -- production France Eastern 2.9 + Western 1.2 = 4.1 = France Germany, area 4.0 + 2.0 = 6.0 -- as do both supporting absences: zero bare `Germany` labels in the hemp table and `France` present separately at 3.9. But this entry records 'AFFECTED: 6 rows (2 per label)', which counts only the 1934-1938 triple carrying the arithmetic. `Western` ALSO appears at 1949, 1950 and 1951 on both indicators -- 8 `Western` rows in total, not 2 -- so TWELVE rows in the table carry one of the three glued labels. Those extra six are the same label defect (a sub-row that kept no prefix at all, which this entry identifies as the inconsistency in the extraction) but they sit outside the identity, so a repair keyed on the 1934-1938 arithmetic would leave them behind. The re-test pins 12 rather than 6.

label: czech republic; serbia; canada; russian federation

summary: 13 INDIVIDUALLY ATTRIBUTABLE defective cells, and unlike almost everything else in this file they are REPAIRABLE, because the correct value is known. Method: two labels that route to the same polity make two sources directly comparable; where they agree to within 1% on 70%+ of at least 8 shared years, they demonstrably measure the same thing, so a cell where they diverge by more than 2x is the defect rather than a difference of scope -- and the agreeing side supplies the value. A bare ratio cannot do this: it tells you two sources disagree, not which is wrong. iia `czech republic` vs juan `czechoslovakia`: rye (ha) 19/23 years agree, diverging 1939 (iia 98,000 vs juan 984,000), 1940 (78,000 vs 708,000), 1941 (78,000 vs 784,000), 1943 (26,000 vs 926,000); rye (tonnes) 18/23 agree, diverging 1942 (29,500 vs 1,231,000), 1943 (36,000 vs 1,536,000), 1944 (32,500 vs 1,214,000), 1945 (28,000 vs 981,000); flax fibre and tow (ha) 20/23 agree, diverging 1942 only (4,000 vs 43,000). iia `serbia` vs juan `yugoslav sfr`: rye (ha) 15/17 agree, diverging 1931 (24,415 vs 244,150) and 1932 (24,296 vs 242,961) -- both EXACTLY one tenth, 244,150/10 = 24,415 and 242,961/10 = 24,296.1; rye (tonnes) 17/18 agree, diverging 1945 where iia is the LARGER side (979,900 vs 92,000); rapeseed (tonnes) 15/16 agree, diverging 1920 (1,929 vs 3,900, x2.0). SHAPE: most divergences are near-exact powers of ten in one direction or the other, i.e. dropped or added digits in single cells, not a systematic rescaling -- the surrounding years match to the digit (czech rye 1930: iia 1,046,335 vs juan 1,046,335 exactly). The czech rye TONNES block 1942-1945 is the exception at x35-43 and is not a clean digit shift. NOT ESTABLISHED: which side is wrong in each case. The agreeing years prove the two measure one thing; they do not prove the majority is right. For czech rye the juan values are plausible for Czechoslovak rye (~700k-1M ha) and iia's 26,000-98,000 ha are not, so iia is the defective side there. serbia rye 1945 runs the other way and iia is the implausible one at 979,900 t. Each cell needs that check before it is repaired. CORRECTED 2026-08-18, SAME DAY: the 'dropped or added digits' reading above is WRONG for the czech cells, and so is the scope-flipping reading queued for the F51-1938-1945 wiki page. Inspecting the raw IIA extract directly, the `czechoslovakia` 1938-1945 block is internally corrupt: for RYE, either the area or the production value is implausible in 7 of the 8 years, and a yield check says which. 1938 reads 1,016,000 ha / 1,906,100 t = 1.88 t/ha, consistent. 1939 reads 98,000 ha / 1,729,400 t = 17.6 t/ha, so the AREA is the wrong cell. 1942 reads 861,000 ha / 29,500 t = 0.03 t/ha, so the PRODUCTION is the wrong cell; likewise 1944 (915,000 / 32,500) and 1945 (802,000 / 28,000). 1943 reads 26,000 ha / 36,000 t, internally consistent at 1.38 t/ha but both figures far too small for Czechoslovak rye. So the defective values are not digit-shifted versions of the truth -- they are numbers attached to the wrong (item, variable) slot in the extraction, which is why the two sides of the same year disagree with each other and not just with juan. The scope-flipping explanation is separately REFUTED: raw `german bohemia and moravia` exists but carries only butter, cheese and milk (21 rows, 1939-1945) and NO rye, so there is no sub-component rye series for the label to alternate with. Same block, same shape, other items: `tobacco` 1939 reads 6,000 ha with 933,000 t, and `hops` 1939 reads 10,500 ha with 763,400 t -- both the x100 defect already logged as iia-tobacco-implausible-magnitudes and iia-hops-x100. And the czech `flax fibre and tow` 1942 cell (4,000 vs juan's 43,000) is NOT a digit drop either: raw carries `flax: fibre` area 43,000 and `linseed` area 4,000 for 1942, so layer B took the LINSEED figure -- the conflation already logged as iia-flax-fibre-item-is-mostly-linseed. WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: the serbia cells. 1931 (24,415 vs 244,150) and 1932 (24,296 vs 242,961) are still exact tenths, and no area/production misalignment is involved. The method also survives -- cross-source agreement on the surrounding years is what made these cells attributable at all -- but attributing them to a digit shift was reading a mechanism off a ratio. ADDED 2026-08-20, a 14th attributable cell and the first in this entry from a DIFFERENT source volume: iia `canada` / eggs, hen, in shell / tonnes / 1930 reads 148.7640 t where the correct value is almost certainly 148,764 t -- the same digits, shifted by 1000. The proof is internal to one volume: iia_1933_34 itself prints 146,658.666 for 1929, 153,376.3308 for 1931 and 148,415.3748 for 1932, so 148.764 sits three orders of magnitude below its own immediate neighbours in the same table, and 146,659 / 148.764 = 985.8. Canada produced roughly 150 kt of eggs a year through the interwar period; 149 TONNES is a village. THIS IS RAW-SIDE, not a consolidation error: the 148.7640 appears in the raw extract exactly as layer B carries it, so no multiplier was applied or lost downstream. ALREADY DETECTED: series_collapses.csv flags it as `interior_collapse` at factor 985.8 against the 1929 neighbour, so the screen was working -- what was missing is the repairable verdict, which this entry exists to hold. Unlike the czech rye cells corrected above, no (item, variable) misalignment is involved: the year, item and unit are all right and only the magnitude is wrong, which is why the digits recover the value. ADDED 2026-08-20, a 15th cell, and the only one in this entry whose correct value is DERIVED FROM THE SOURCE'S OWN ARITHMETIC rather than inferred from neighbours: iia `russian federation` / rye / tonnes / 1931 reads 21,990 t where it should read 21,990,000 t. iia_1933_34 prints two aggregate rows for the same year -- `total general including the ussr` 43,358,000 and `total general excluding the ussr` 21,368,000 -- whose DIFFERENCE is 21,990,000, i.e. the USSR's own rye production, exactly 1000x the printed cell. The neighbours agree independently: raw `ussr` rye is 23,600,000 (1930), 22,020,000 (1932) and 24,190,000 (1933), so 21,990,000 sits among them and 21,990 is three orders below. THE UNIT HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED: I first read this as thousand-tonnes beside tonnes within one series, because the convention at (iia, russian federation, *) establishes that label as whole-USSR scope and a mixed-unit series was the obvious explanation. The aggregate difference rules it out -- the source's own total is in tonnes and its residual is 21,990,000, so the cell is a decimal shift, not a unit. ALREADY DETECTED, like the canada cell above: series_collapses.csv carries it as `interior_collapse`, value 21990, neighbour 2.202e+07, factor 1001.4 -- and note the factor is 1001.4 rather than 1000 precisely because the neighbour is 1932's 22,020,000 rather than the true 1931 value, which is why a neighbour ratio cannot supply a repair and the aggregate difference can.

These are the only two of the 21 that can be settled that way. iia india sesame seed (ha): 1,000 repeated for 1934-1945, against a median of 2,208,440 for the same series' other 8 values -- a ratio of 0.00045, i.e. the constant is ~2,200x too small. India's sesame area really was ~2.5M ha, so 1,000 ha is not a rounding of anything. iia new zealand tobacco unmanufactured (ha): 1,000 repeated for 1934-1945 against a median of 83 for the series' other 9 values -- 12x too large, and New Zealand's interwar tobacco acreage was in the tens of hectares. NOT REPAIRABLE by rescaling: the correct values are unknown, and for india the surrounding years give 2.0-2.5M ha, so the run should read NA rather than any number. WHY THE OTHER 19 ARE NOT LISTED HERE. 12 of them repeat a value within 2x of their own series' median, so the figure is plausible in magnitude and only its flatness is wrong -- repetition and placeholder are indistinguishable from the panel. Two are demonstrably CARRIED FORWARD (the constant equals the last observed value before the run: argentina soybeans 1,000 against 992, denmark potatoes 54,000 against 54,100) and four are consistent with INTERPOLATION (the constant lies between the flanking values). Those six are defects of method rather than of magnitude. See issue #366 for the full classification. FIGURES HAVE DRIFTED, MEASURED 2026-08-21, AND ARE NOT RE-TESTED YET. Re-measuring the two series over all their cells: iia india sesame seed (ha) has 12 cells at 1,000 against 10 other values with a median of 2,142,517 -- this entry records 8 other values with a median of 2,208,440. iia new zealand tobacco unmanufactured (ha) has 13 cells at 1,000 against 10 others with a median of 254 -- this entry records 9 others with a median of 83, so the comparison ratio moves from 12x too large to 3.9x too large. The DIRECTION of both is unchanged and the conclusion stands (1,000 is orders away from India's real sesame area, and is above rather than below New Zealand's tobacco scale), but the entry's medians are computed over a population this measurement does not reproduce -- probably dated rows only, as with two other entries whose denominators were recovered that way. NOT PINNED IN 35_retest_data_errors.py until that filter is identified: pinning a median whose population is unknown would be a check that passes for the wrong reason.

label: united states of america; canada; argentina
summary: RESOLVES issue #360's two largest recorded source seams, and NOT by the mechanism that issue proposed. `united states / flax fibre and tow / ha` jumps x1655 at a juan->mitchell boundary and Canada x1231; #360 offered a unit or thousands-multiplier mismatch as the leading candidate. It is neither: MITCHELL'S VALUES UNDER `flax fibre and tow` ARE LINSEED AREA. Proof is exact equality with juan's own separately-labelled linseed series for the same country: united states 1950 mitchell flax-fibre 1,655,000 ha == juan linseed 1,655,000; 1952 mitchell 1,337,000 == juan 1,337,000; 1900 and 1901 likewise. canada 1952 mitchell 469,000 == juan linseed 469,000 (at 1951, the crop-year offset). Across the whole panel, 55 of the 204 mitchell `flax fibre and tow` (ha) values exactly equal a juan LINSEED (ha) value for the same country, against just 1 of 204 that equals a juan FLAX FIBRE AND TOW value -- a 55:1 ratio against the control, which rules out coincidence as the account of the bulk. Some of the 55 sit at a +/-1 year offset, which is the southern-hemisphere crop-year convention (argentina mitchell 1911 == juan 1912, and so on through 1922). THE YIELD IDENTITY CORROBORATES INDEPENDENTLY. juan's US flax-fibre series runs 3,000 ha and 1,900 t (1945) down to 1,000 ha and 400 t (1949), i.e. 0.30-0.63 t/ha, which is fibre flax. Mitchell's 1,655,000 ha against juan's 1950 fibre production of 100 t would imply 0.00006 t/ha. US linseed yields 0.46-0.70 t/ha across the same years, which is what these areas belong to. SCOPE: this is the same conflation already logged as iia-flax-fibre-item-is-mostly-linseed, now shown to affect MITCHELL as well as IIA -- so it is a property of how the item was harmonised rather than of one source. Not repairable by rescaling: the affected cells need re-attributing to `linseed`, and 27% is a floor on the share affected rather than an estimate, because it counts only cells whose value survives to be matched exactly.

IDENTIFIED 2026-08-20, ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN THE LABEL'S NAME: `[error] inde` IS BRITISH INDIA. The earlier entry said this could not be claimed because the cells match nothing; that was wrong -- 26 of the block's 414 production/area rows DO have a `british india` counterpart, and where both report the same product, year, unit and variable the values agree within edition-revision noise: guano natural 4,700 vs 4,710 (0.998), tea area 331,000 vs 330,000 (1.003), cottonseed 2,116,300 vs 2,101,060 (1.007), rapeseed production 613,700 vs 617,800 (0.993), groundnut production 3,237,100 vs 3,286,910 (0.985), tobacco area 471,000 vs 490,500 (0.960), groundnut area 3,070,000 vs 3,284,000 (0.935), sesame production 481,600 vs 543,600 (0.886) -- eight of nine within 7%. ALL the overlapping cells are at 1933, which is where they should be, since 1933 is the only year two volumes cover. Provenance corroborates: the block is entirely iia_1938_39 (245 rows) and iia_1939_45 (204), spanning 1933-1945, i.e. the late-volume India series with a broken country label. So 388 of its 414 rows are non-duplicating British India production/area cells. RECOVERY IS NOT CLEAN: its tobacco production reads 38.2-64.9 MILLION tonnes on 412,000-539,000 ha, i.e. 124 t/ha, which is impossible and becomes an ordinary 1.24 t/ha divided by 100 -- the x100 era defect of iia-tobacco-implausible-magnitudes and iia-hops-x100, so importing the block without that remedy imports 15 inflated cells. That also confirms the 1933 mechanism directly: the raw iia_1938_39 figure AT 1933 is inflated, and 1933 is clean in layer B only because iia_1933_34 supplies a second opinion the pipeline prefers. NOT A DEFECT OF THIS REPO: the corruption is upstream in the extract, so the open question is whether to record the loss (as #414 does for blank-as-zero) and whether the legible subset is worth recovering by hand; the togo/cameroun mandate rows are territories this database has a live interest in. Found while generalising #422's Karafuto test. See issue #493. THE CAMEROUN BLOCK IS VERIFIED THE SAME WAY, 2026-08-20, and it passes a check the togo block cannot. AND IT CORROBORATES THE VOLUME MODEL INDEPENDENTLY: the block's tobacco rows are 1930-1932, inside iia_1933_34's window, and read 49.3 / 42.2 / 109.0 t -- clean-volume magnitudes with NO x100. Were the block mis-assembled from late volumes those figures would be inflated a hundredfold, as `[error] inde`'s tobacco is. RECOVERABLE SET: `[error] inde` 388 cells (British India, identified), `[error] togo*` 45, `[error] cameroun*` 37, `syrie/liban` 21, `palestine` 10. CLASS COMPLETE 2026-08-20. Across the class the model makes three different predictions and matches all three: `[error] inde` (late volumes, has tobacco) IS x100 inflated; `[error] cameroun` (early volumes, has tobacco) is NOT; syrie/liban and palestine (late volumes, no tobacco) are plausible. None of the blocks was examined in order to test it. FINAL RECOVERABLE SET: inde 388 cells, togo 45, cameroun 37, syrie/liban 21, palestine 12 = 503 production/area cells, every block complementary, internally coherent and consistent with what its years imply about its source volume. SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-21, on re-test: the variable split above is not a partition. label: China
commodity: pigs; buffaloes; meat; wool clean basis; slaughter fats other than pig
summary: SIX CELLS UNDER fao1952's `China` LABEL CARRY IMPLAUSIBLY SMALL VALUES, while the label itself is a correct national total -- so this is per-cell damage, NOT a mislabelled or misrouted series. Issue #449 concluded from pigs and buffaloes that 'the China figure is not a national total ... the two labels are not the same territory'; that label-level conclusion is NOT supported. THE LABEL IS CHINA: use total 973,629 (1000 ha) = 9.74 million km2, China's land area; population total 452,460 (1937) and 463,500 (1951) thousand people; use land 944,420, built-on/wasteland 604,456, permanent pasture 194,133, arable 91,040; oats 730-792 kt on 940-959 kha; wool greasy basis 40/40/30 kt. The whole/parts relation is also right: use total reads China 973,629 against `China 22 provinces` 507,182, i.e. the parts are 52% of the whole, exactly what is expected when the 22 provinces exclude Manchuria, Tibet, Sinkiang and Mongolia. THE BROKEN CELLS: pigs 1949 = 95 against `China 22 provinces` 59,510 (China's 1949 herd was about 58 million head); buffaloes 1949 = 658 against 9,460 (about 9.5 million); buffaloes 1950 = 656 and 1951 = 568; meat 1950 = 1 and 1951 = 3 (1000 tonnes, for a nation); wool clean basis 1951 = 1 against 22 in both 1949 and 1950; slaughter fats other than pig 1948 = 30 against the 22 provinces' 1. NO SINGLE UNIT ERROR EXPLAINS THEM, which is the argument for per-cell treatment: pigs x1000 gives 95 million, above the 22 provinces' 59.5 million and plausible; but buffaloes x1000 gives 658 million against a WORLD buffalo population of roughly 45 million, x100 gives 65.8 million which is still above the world total, and x10 gives 6.58 million which is now BELOW the 22 provinces' 9.46 million. Every multiplier fails. NOT REPAIRABLE: the 22-provinces figure is a lower bound on the national one, not a substitute for it, so unlike iia-attributable-single-cell-errors no correct value is recoverable from within the panel. The consumer averages rather than sums duplicate keys, so a cell holding both the whole and a part publishes a blend; see layerb-nested-reporting-levels-one-polity for that population. See issue #449.
