label: reunion (raw: french reunion); romania
summary: TEN FALSE EXONERATIONS IN era_shift_verdicts.csv, caused by a baseline drawn from the inflated volume. The era screen convicts a no-area row when it is >=30x the label's OWN pre-1934 median. For `reunion` that median is 20,000 t, which is itself an inflated figure, so every era row divides one inflated number by another and reads as consistent: ratio_to_own 1.00 for 1934/1935/1936 and 0.76-1.11 for 1939-1945, all filed no_area_level_consistent and none convicted. THE RAW SERIES SHOWS THE TRUTH: french reunion tobacco production reads 423.1 t (1926) and 348.4 t (1927) from iia_1929_30, then 20,000 t at 1933 and 1934-1936 from iia_1938_39, then 15,200-22,300 for 1939-1945 from iia_1939_45. A few hundred tonnes to 20,000 is a 47x step at 1933. Reunion is 2,512 km2, so a few hundred tonnes is the plausible figure and 20,000 is not. WHY THE 1933 SECOND OPINION DID NOT RESCUE IT: iia_1933_34 carries NO DATED 1933 production for this label -- only an undated 670.8 t row -- so there was nothing to outvote the late volume, the inflated figure filled 1933, and it became the baseline for every later year. THE CONDITION IS BROADER THAN THAT, established by a second case: `romania` / hops is contaminated too even though iia_1933_34 DOES supply a clean dated 1933 (9.5 t on 2 ha, beside 29.9 / 48.3 / 15.1 t for 1930-1932). Its recorded baseline is 1,770, which is exactly (3,500 + 40.6) / 2 -- the mean of the clean `1925-1929` period row from iia_1933_34 and the INFLATED `1928-1932` period row from iia_1938_39. Because the era baseline includes pre-era PERIOD rows, one inflated period row contaminates it regardless of how many clean dated years exist. So the general condition is that a pre-1934 baseline is clean only where EVERY pre-era row feeding it -- dated or period -- comes from a volume without the x100, not merely where a dated 1933 exists. That makes romania hops 1934-1938 an eleventh false exoneration on the same mechanism. NOT A THRESHOLD PROBLEM: the other ten no_area_level_consistent rows sit at 3.2x to 27.1x their own baseline and are simply under the 30x line (jordan 27.1, mauritania 25.0), which is a conservative-line question rather than a contaminated one. The 348 convictions are unaffected. See issue #416. RE-TESTED 2026-08-21. The mechanism reproduces exactly: reunion's ten exonerations, its 20,000 baseline, the 1.00 ratios at 1934-1936, and -- the load-bearing one -- romania/hops' recorded baseline of 1770.3, which is (3,500 + 40.6) / 2 to the digit. Two counts have drifted, and the second is not a count. THE OTHER TEN ARE ELEVEN, and the eleventh is not in the stated 3.2x-27.1x band: `germany / tobacco, unmanufactured / 1945` sits at ratio 0.0 -- a ZERO production filed no_area_level_consistent. So the sentence 'the other ten sit at 3.2x to 27.1x, which is a conservative-line question rather than a contaminated one' is right about ten of the eleven and wrong about the kind of the twelfth case. THE SCREEN'S LEVEL TEST IS ONE-SIDED: it convicts at >=30x its own baseline and exonerates everything below, so a value cannot be too SMALL to fail. That row also escapes the impossible_yield_zero_area arm, because that arm requires area == 0 and this row's area is BLANK, not zero -- the same blank-vs-zero distinction issue 414 is about. Exposure is exactly one row: the only other cells at <=0.34x their own baseline are micronesia's two (0.148 and 0.296), and both ARE convicted, by the zero-area arm. So this is a real one-sided test with a single live cell, which is worth stating as that rather than as a class. Also convicted rows are 349, not 348. All figures are now pinned by check_reunion_tobacco_baseline in 35_retest_data_errors.py. THE SIBLING ONE-SIDED-TEST GAP IS FIXED, THIS ENTRY'S OWN DEFECT IS NOT (2026-08-31, PR #603). The re-test for this entry had surfaced an ELEVENTH exonerated row outside the 3.2x-27.1x band described above -- `germany / tobacco / 1945`, a ZERO production at ratio 0.0 filed no_area_level_consistent, because the screen convicted only at >=30x and so a value could not be too SMALL to pass. #603 added the low side of that ratio test as the verdict `no_area_level_drop` and the row is now convicted, which moved five recorded counts (no_area_level_consistent 22->21, others 11->10, their lowest ratio 0.0->3.211009, exonerated-not-convicted 1->0, convicted 349->350). THE BAND ABOVE IS THEREBY RESTORED: the ten remaining exonerations span exactly 3.211009 to 27.100271, so this entry's stated range was right all along and the drift was one row that did not belong in the class. Reunion's own ten exonerations are untouched and this defect stays open -- each still divides one inflated number by another against the 20,000 t baseline.

label: `Leeward Islands  Trinidad and Tobago` (6 rows); `Jamaica Trinidad and Tobago` (1)
commodity: land use (use total, arable, pastures, forests, builton); irrigation
summary: TWO fao1952 labels attach a territory to a colonial GROUPING IT WAS NEVER IN, and the defect is in the heading rather than the territory. `Leeward Islands  Trinidad and Tobago` carries 6 land-use rows at 1951 and `Jamaica Trinidad and Tobago` 1 irrigation row at 1951; Trinidad and Tobago was neither a Leeward Island nor part of Jamaica. fao1952 carries SEVEN label variants for this one territory (british west indies trinidad and tobago 49 rows, british west indies trinidad & tobago 10, leeward islands trinidad and tobago 6, british w indies trinidad and tobago 4, br w indies trinidad and tobago 3, trinidad and tobago 3, jamaica trinidad and tobago 1), and all seven route to TTO-1800-2025, so no value lands on the wrong polity. WHICH HALF OF THE LABEL IS WRONG IS DECIDABLE, and the innocent reading is the dangerous one: if the heading were right and the TERRITORY had bled in from an adjacent row, the 513 thousand ha would belong to the Leeward Islands and be a wrong value rather than a wrong label. It does not. 513 thousand ha = 5,130 km2, and Trinidad and Tobago is 5,128 km2; the Leeward Islands are about 1,000 km2, and this source's own `leeward islands` row reads `use total` 109 thousand ha = 1,090 km2. So the value is Trinidad's, the territory name is correct, and only the group heading is spurious. NOT A DOUBLE COUNT: merging the two mis-parented labels against the five correctly-parented ones on (item, indicator, year, unit) gives 0 colliding cells, so these 7 rows are observations the other labels do not carry -- dropping them would lose data, and summing them alongside is safe. THE MECHANISM IS VISIBLE IN THE SEPARATOR. fao1952 labels are a group heading concatenated with a territory, and the concatenation shows as a DOUBLE SPACE: `British West Indies  Barbados`, `Germany  Western`, `France  Saar`, and here `Leeward Islands  Trinidad and Tobago`. In the correct cases the heading is the territory's actual group; in these two it is the wrong one, which is what a heading picked up from the wrong table row or column looks like. WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE ROUTING CORRECTLY: the label text is the input to every prefix- and containment-based screen, so a wrong heading manufactures a false hierarchy -- it put a fourth 'child' under `leeward islands` in label_hierarchy_identity.csv (#519). This class differs from iia-corrupted-country-labels, which is OCR damage that is unreadable and obviously broken; these are READABLE AND WRONG, so nothing downstream looks amiss. UPSTREAM, NOT A DEFECT OF THIS REPO: the label text comes from the fao1952 extraction, and the repo's aliases already route all seven variants correctly, so there is nothing here to repair locally -- the entry records the defect so a prefix-based screen can exclude it and so the 7 rows are not mistaken for Leeward Islands or Jamaica data. Found while explaining a subset verdict in #519; reported on issue 450.

label: Korea (peninsula); compared against Korea South
summary: fao1952 `Korea` rice paddy AREA at period 1934-1938 reads 645 thousand ha while `Korea South` reads 1,216 -- a PART exceeding its WHOLE. `Korea` is the whole peninsula and `Korea South` the ROK: proven by the source's own arithmetic at 1949, where nitrogenous fertilizer consumption reads Korea 108.9 = Korea South 98.9 + Korea North 10.0 exactly, and corroborated by population 1951 (Korea 29,300 thousand vs Korea South 20,500, against a ROK population of about 20.5M in a peninsula of about 29M). THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS, and the third is what pins the AREA cell rather than the scope. (1) Of the 17 1934-1938 cells carrying both labels, this is the ONLY one where the part exceeds the whole; the other 16 run 0.043 to 1.000, and their spread is agronomically sensible for a north-south split (oats 0.043 and rye 0.111 concentrated in the north, rice production 0.737 in the south). (2) The implied yield is impossible: 3,699 kt on 645 kha is 5.73 t/ha, against 2.24 for Korea South's own 2,726/1,216 and a 1930s paddy-rice range of roughly 2.0-3.0 t/ha. At an area near 1,600 kha the yield would be 2.31, which is in band; Korea's total paddy area in the 1930s was of that order. (3) THE SAME ITEM'S PRODUCTION ROW IS CONSISTENT: 3,699 vs 2,726 is a ratio of 0.737, exactly what a whole-peninsula figure beside a southern one should look like. So the scope of the label is not in question for this item -- only the area figure is, which is why this is a single-cell defect and not a scope finding. NO REMEDY IS ASSERTED: 1,600 kha is inferred from the yield and from the production ratio, not read from a source, and the fao1952 raw extract is not in this repository so the printed page cannot be checked here. CONSEQUENCE: any yield computed for KOR-1800-1945 from this pair is 2.5x too high, and any check that tests a part against its whole sees one violation on this pair that has nothing to do with the peninsula/ROK routing question. Found while resolving issue 355's Korea case; reported there.

label: russian federation (from `russia in europe` + `russia in asia`)
commodity: tobacco, unmanufactured (8 cells); rye (2); sugar raw centrifugal (1)
summary: layer-B `iia` / `russian federation` is built by SUMMING the raw labels `russia in europe` and `russia in asia` for the pre-Soviet years, and for one item the Asian component is dropped in EVERY year it exists. Measured 2026-08-20 over every cell whose year carries both components in the raw extract: 72 cells sum correctly (within 2% of europe+asia), 11 equal the EUROPEAN component alone, 6 are explained otherwise. THE 11: tobacco, unmanufactured (production, tonnes) at 1909 81,381.5 / 1910 72,634.5 / 1911 112,103.8 / 1912 107,685.2 / 1913 91,620.5 / 1914 82,427.9 / 1915 96,572.1 / 1916 92,029.9 -- every one EXACTLY equal to `russia in europe`, with the Asian component (12,718 / 15,818 / 14,303 / 13,059 / 14,271 / 19,482 / 14,142 / 18,692 t) missing, i.e. understated by 10.8% to 19.1%; rye (ha) 1920 = 17,017,242 exactly europe, missing 877,574 ha (4.9%); rye (ha) 1917 = 9,993,626 against europe 9,993,613, i.e. europe to within 13 ha out of 10 million; and sugar raw centrifugal 1911, real but negligible at 0.06% (Asian sugar 1,170 t against 1.97 million). EXACT EQUALITY IS THE LOAD-BEARING EVIDENCE, not the size of the gap: an approximate match to one component would be consistent with a revision or a different volume, whereas equality to the digit in eight consecutive years says the component was never added. THE SECOND LEG is that the summing logic demonstrably WORKS for this same label -- 72 cells sum both components correctly -- so this is a per-item omission and not an absence of summing. NOT TO BE CONFUSED with the continental-half boundary in the source_conventions entry for this label: there the published value IS a half and the label claims the whole; here two halves are summed for 72 cells and one is forgotten for 11. SCOPE: pre-Soviet years only (1909-1920), where the two continental components exist as raw labels; says nothing about the whole-USSR years. UPSTREAM, NOT A DEFECT OF THIS REPO: the summing happens in the layer-B build, so there is nothing to reroute or repair locally. NO REMEDY ASSERTED -- whether the fix is to add the Asian component or to publish the two separately is a layer-B decision. Tobacco is also the item carrying the x100 era defect (iia-tobacco-implausible-magnitudes), but that is a different mechanism in a different year range (1934-1945) and no connection is claimed beyond the coincidence of item. Found by testing an incidental claim on issue 422 that this label is 'otherwise europe + asia summed'; reported on issue 315. A TRAP FOR ANYONE RE-DERIVING THIS: `russia in asia` is itself a multi-row label. For rye it carries TWO rows in each of 1909-1916 (918,720 and 318,737 at 1909; 848,436 and 325,913 at 1910) and one in 1917 and 1920, so the correct early sum is THREE-term -- 28,161,536 + 918,720 + 318,737 = 29,398,993, which is issue 422's identity seen from the other side. Taking one row per year understates the component by about 3% and makes the correctly-summed years look wrong too; that is exactly what happened on the first pass of this entry's own re-test, which reported 0 correctly-summed rye cells instead of 8. Tobacco's Asian component IS single-row per year, so the eight figures quoted above are unaffected.

label: british nigeria; french equatorial africa; dominican republic; british uganda (raw labels)
summary: 11 dated zeros in iia_1939_45 that the volume's OWN REPORTING GRID cannot produce, proved cell-locally by the other half of the same cell. THE TEST. iia_1938_39 and iia_1939_45 print hectares on a 1000-grid (4,632 of 4,634 and 6,083 of 6,311 non-zero values are exact multiples) and tonnes on a 100-grid (8,314 of 8,991; 9,514 of 10,235), against 3.6%-19.0% (hectares on 1000) and 11.7%-26.4% (tonnes on 100) in the four earlier volumes -- so in those two volumes a 0 is also the only way to write any area below 500 ha or any tonnage below 50 t, and most of their zeros are a resolution floor rather than a blank (issue 446). That floor puts an arithmetic BOUND on the implied yield: a zero area means yield > production/(grid/2), a zero production means yield < (grid/2)/area. When the bound is an order of magnitude outside the volume's OWN 10th-90th percentile yield band for the same product, no sub-grid value produces the pair and the zero is false. The band is measured on the same volume and product, so a uniform per-item scale error cancels -- which is what makes the test usable inside issue 416's x100 tobacco era, where iia_1939_45's own median tobacco yield is 82.6 t/ha. THE 11 CELLS. british nigeria / cotton: ginned / area = 0 for 1939, 1940, 1941, 1942, 1943, 1944 against lint production of 9,200 / 13,300 / 6,600 / 5,900 / 4,500 / 2,900 t, implying minimum yields of 5.8-26.6 t/ha against a band of 0.067-0.339 (17x-78x outside); french equatorial africa / cotton: ginned / area = 0 for 1939 against 8,800 t (52x); dominican republic / tobacco / area = 0 for 1939 against 871,400 t (12x); british uganda / tobacco / production = 0 for 1942, 1943, 1944 against areas of 5,000 / 5,000 / 3,000 ha, implying maximum yields of 0.010-0.017 t/ha against a band of 33.1-145.4 (1,985x-3,308x outside). The nigeria cells for 1941-1945 are already registered as nga-1941-1945-cotton-area-zero on the cotton-seed tonnage beside them; 1939 and 1940 are new, and the whole series is 7 zeros of 7 with the area never once positive in the volume. LAYER-B EXPOSURE is 9 rows, all is_aggregate=False: nigeria cotton lint ha 1939-1945 (7 zeros, the entire series), congo cotton lint ha 1939 = 0 where the same volume's 1934-1938 average is 154,000 ha, and dominican republic tobacco, unmanufactured ha, whose whole panel record is 1925-1929 = 16,000 and 1939 = 0 (a two-observation series whose mean is halved by the zero). british uganda tobacco does not reach layer B at all, so those 3 cells are a raw-side defect only -- they must not arrive with the zeros if the label is ever matched. WHAT THIS ENTRY ALSO PINS IS A NEGATIVE. iia_1938_39, the volume issue 414 is named after and the source of 940 of the extract's 1,102 production/area zeros, holds 278 of the 291 testable cells and NOT ONE of them is refuted: 253 grid_can_explain, 23 no_product_reference (all 23 citrus, with implied minimum yields of 0.2-14.2 t/ha against the volume's own citrus fruits: lemons band of 5.5-18.1, so a sibling reference would place all 23 inside it), and 2 where the PRODUCTION is the outlier rather than the zero (french guadeloupe cottonseed 1934 at 3,884,600 t, 53,581x its own series median in that volume; british antigua cottonseed 1934 at 14,400 t, 72x). For the other 251 an area below 500 ha is arithmetically compatible with the tonnage printed beside it. A regression that turns any of those 251 into a refutation, or drops one of the 11, changes this entry. NOT CONFIRMED HERE, AND WHY. A second test compares a zero against the volume's own period-average row for the identical series -- same volume, same grid, no scale confound -- and fires on 30 series / 105 zero-years. It is not usable, because its largest hit is a trap: new zealand fertilizers: phosphate, natural reads 0 for 1926 and 1927 in iia_1929_30 against a 1921-1925 average of 11,176 t, a 112-step contradiction, but the same series runs 3,178 -> 2,421 -> 1,600 in 1922-1924 and the 11,176 is a stale figure re-printed from iia_1925_26's 1909-1913 average. Those zeros are the end of a monotone decline and are probably right. Its trailing-edge cases are real defects of PUBLISHED VALUE but not of this class: estonia milk: cow production 1944 = 0 against a 1934-1938 average of 1,652,000 t (layer B carries exactly those two rows, so the panel mean is 826,000), latvia cheese: factory 1940 = 0 against 1,100 t, british malta eggs 1939 = 0 against 3,611.3 t, and `total general including the ussr` linseed area 1943-1945 = 0 against a 7,680,000 ha world average. `Not separately reported under occupation` and `blank read as 0` are not separable from the numbers, and neither is a rounding. Tool: 40_zero_grid_floor.py, table state/zero_grid_floor.csv.

label: Estates (the area half of `Indonesia Estates`)
summary: The fao1952 country label `Estates` is NOT A TERRITORY -- it is the AREA half of `Indonesia Estates`, whose country prefix was lost, and issue 450 recorded it as a label it 'cannot identify at all'. The two labels carry the same item over the same four reporting periods with complementary indicators, and the YIELD IDENTITY is what identifies it rather than the name: `Indonesia Estates` holds coffee crops:production in 1000 tonnes (1934-1938 55.6; 1949 10.9; 1950 11.1; 1951 12.0) and `Estates` holds coffee crops:area in 1000 hectares (1934-1938 113.0; 1949 33.0; 1950 41.0; 1951 40.0), so the implied yields are 0.492, 0.330, 0.271 and 0.300 t/ha. Coffee at 0.27-0.49 t/ha is ordinary, and an estate area collapsing to a third of its pre-war extent by 1949 is the expected history, so the pairing is corroborated by agronomy and not merely by the two labels sitting near each other. Neither label routes: both are 0 of 4. WHY THIS IS NOT A FREE ALIAS FIX, which is the point of recording it. `Indonesia` itself routes 144 of 144 and carries its own 4 coffee rows, so `Indonesia Estates` is a TENURE SUB-CATEGORY OF A TOTAL THAT ALREADY LANDS. Routing the estate rows onto the same polity reproduces the total-beside-parts collision of iia/fao1952 recorded elsewhere in this file and in issues 367, 411 and 449 -- and the R consumer collapses duplicate keys with mean() rather than choosing the total, so the published figure would fall between the national total and its estate component instead of equalling either. The repair therefore needs the same decision those issues need, and the label's identity -- established here -- is only the first half of it. Three sibling labels look like the same structural bleed of a table's own heading into the country column and are NOT identified: `Western` (13 rows), `Eastern` (5) and `Commercial product` (5).

label: Western; Eastern (Germany's occupation zones)
summary: The fao1952 country labels `Western` (13 rows) and `Eastern` (5 rows) are GERMANY'S OCCUPATION ZONES with the `Germany ` prefix lost, and an ADDITIVE IDENTITY proves it to the digit on two independent variables. Agricultural population (1000 people): 1937 Germany 13,145 against Western 10,091 + Eastern 3,037 = 13,128, residual +17; 1951 Germany 11,601 against Western 8,096 + Eastern 3,488 = 11,584, residual +17. Goats (1000 head): 1949 Germany 2,831 against 1,428 + 1,398 = 2,826; 1950 3,094 against 1,445 + 1,644 = 3,089; 1951 2,962 against 1,347 + 1,610 = 2,957 -- residual +5 in every year. FIVE YEAR-OBSERVATIONS, TEN DISTINCT COMPONENT VALUES, AND THE RESIDUAL IS CONSTANT WITHIN EACH VARIABLE while differing between them (+17 people, +5 goats), which is what a genuine third component looks like rather than a coincidence or a rounding artefact; `Germany Berlin` exists with 42 rows and is the obvious candidate, though the panel carries no Berlin agricultural-population row so the residual is confirmed constant rather than confirmed to BE Berlin. A coincidence would have to reproduce the same offset across a 14-year gap on one variable and three consecutive years on another. NEITHER LABEL ROUTES (0 of 13 and 0 of 5) while the correctly-prefixed twins route completely: `Germany Western` 254 of 254 and `Germany Eastern` 109 of 109. MOST OF IT IS EXECUTABLE, AND THE SPLIT IS EXACT. For 1949-1951 the twins route to F78-1949-1990 and F77-1949-1990 while the `Germany` total routes to DEU-1949-1990, so total and parts land on DIFFERENT polities and there is no collision; the orphan rows also share ZERO (item, indicator, unit, year, period) keys with their twins, so they are new data and not duplicates. 14 of the 18 rows fall there. The other 4 -- two `1934-1938` hemp rows and the two 1937 agricultural-population rows -- route to DEU-1920-1938, the SAME polity the `Germany` total uses for those years, which is issue 411's recorded total-and-parts defect, and the consumer collapses such keys with mean() rather than choosing the total. So the awkward rows are again the back-projected ones, as with fao1952-estates-label-lost-country-prefix and with issue 450's main class of 95. Not routed here: routing changes published aggregates and belongs in its own reviewed change. ROUTED, PARTIALLY (2026-08-31). The 14 non-colliding rows are now aliased: `Western` fao1952 1949-1951 -> F78-1949-1990 (10 rows) and `Eastern` fao1952 1949-1951 -> F77-1949-1990 (4 rows), both scoped to fao1952 and both recorded in applied_aliases.csv with the identity as their basis. Panel routing went 189,995 -> 190,009 of 190,529 and unrouted 534 -> 520; the ONLY cells whose routing changed are those 14, verified by diffing matched_rows.parquet before and after. No published value moved, because every one of the 14 is a new (polity, item, indicator, unit, year) cell and fao1952 is the only source on either polity. THE FOUR BACK-PROJECTED ROWS ARE DELIBERATELY STILL UNROUTED -- `Western` at 1934-1938 and 1937, `Eastern` at 1937 -- because they would land on DEU-1920-1938 beside the `Germany` total, which is issue 411's total-and-parts defect, and the consumer collapses such keys with mean() rather than choosing the total. That is a decision, not an oversight, and the re-test pins WHICH rows remain unrouted by year rather than merely how many, so swapping a 1949 row for a 1937 one cannot pass.

label: algeria (raw: ALGÉRIE / ALGÉRIE french)
summary: THE CIVIL-DEPARTMENTS BASIS RUNS TO DATA YEAR 1925, BUT THE POLITY CREATED FOR IT ENDS AT 1919, so 94 iia rows carry a territory 4.03x too large. PR #605 created DZA-CVD-1902-1919 (declared 575,511 km2) for IIA's Algeria data on the three civil departments, resolving issue 400's case 2 for data years 1902-1918. IIA's OWN STATED AREAS show the basis continuing past that: data_year 1911 575,289; 1913 575,511 and 576,000; 1921 575,289; 1925 575,511; then 1929 2,195,097; 1932 and 1933 2,196,294; 1937 2,204,864; 1951 2,204,860 (data/final/source_stated_areas.csv). So the switch to the whole colony sits between data year 1925 and 1929, and the 94 iia dated rows at 1919-1925 land on DZA-1919-1962 whose polygon is 2,318,386 km2 -- a factor of 4.03 against the ~575,300 km2 the source states for those very years. This is the identical defect #605 documented and repaired, continuing seven data years past the new polity's end. THE BOUNDARY IS GAP-SEPARATED, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT UNAMBIGUOUS: iia has ZERO Algeria rows at 1926, 1927 and 1928, so any boundary in those three years partitions the data identically and the basis change needs no dating by inference. Bands: 1902-1918 17 rows (1917-1918 shown) on DZA-CVD; 1919-1925 94 rows on DZA-1919-1962; 1926-1928 0 rows; 1929-1935 111 rows on DZA-1919-1962, correctly, since the source states the whole colony from 1929. The natural repair is to extend DZA-CVD-1902-1919 to end_year 1926 and widen its alias window to 1925; its declared area is ALREADY the right figure. mitchell has a further 189 rows in the same band, but IIA's stated areas are evidence for IIA only and mitchell's basis is NOT established here. SEPARATELY, 49 PERIOD ROWS STRADDLE THE SWITCH AND NO ROUTING CAN FIX THEM: 1925-1929 (24 rows, printed by iia_1933_34) and 1928-1932 (25 rows, iia_1938_39) are retrospective averages computed ACROSS the territorial redefinition, so they are not attributable to either territory and need a caveat or exclusion rather than a destination. 1909-1913 (19) and 1900-1913 (2) are correctly on DZA-CVD, and 1934-1938 (24) correctly on the whole colony.

label: Germany Western
summary: fao1952 `Germany Western` publishes 2 thousand tonnes of cheese for the 1934-1938 average, two to three orders of magnitude below what the label's own behaviour predicts, and the finding survives the one thing that had blocked it. THE BLOCKER AND WHY IT DOES NOT BIND: `cheese` carries item_code 161_162 -- a RANGE, two FAO codes collapsed into one layer-B item -- so `Germany` holds TWO cheese rows at 1934-1938 (154 and 1,114) and `Germany Western` holds TWO (2 and 2), and issue 411 could not say which pairs with which. But both branches are extreme: 2/154 = 0.013 and 2/1,114 = 0.002. The anomaly therefore survives the ambiguity instead of being blocked by it, which is the correction that made this registerable. THE BASELINE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Across the 22 (item, item_code, indicator, unit) keys where both labels carry exactly one row at 1934-1938, `Germany Western` / `Germany` has median 0.635 and range 0.382-0.749 -- the West German share of the 1937 Reich, reproduced independently by crops, livestock, fertiliser and population (issue 411). So the expected West German cheese figure is about 98 if the 154 pairing is right and about 707 if the 1,114 pairing is, against an observed 2. CORROBORATED THREE MORE WAYS. First, the same label's cheese series continue 149/137/152 and 34/52/74 at 1949-1951, so 2 is out of line with its own later values under either pairing. Second, the share band is not an artefact of key selection: applying the repo's own recorded alphabetical row order for the `poultry` group (11_retest_conventions.py::check_fao1952_poultry_order, verified against `juan`, winning 27 of 28 groups) pairs chickens/ducks/geese at 0.729/0.605/0.598, all inside the band. Third, every key has MATCHING cardinality on both sides, so nothing here is structurally unpairable; the comparable count is 28 cells, median 0.608. NOT DIAGNOSED: a dropped leading digit is the obvious reading and the yearbook page has not been opened, so the CAUSE is not asserted -- only that the published value cannot be right under any available pairing. Related: issue 367 (the collapsed item codes), issue 411 (the territorial-basis collision this was found inside). One residue: `turkeys` order-aligns at 0.236, the only order-aligned cell outside the band, which is either a real east-west distributional fact or a second small-cell defect.

label: (all labels carrying item_code 192_194)
summary: fao1952 item_code 192_194 carries a TOTAL, its two exact COMPONENTS, and a fourth broader measure that is not a component of it -- 952 non-aggregate rows across four layer-B items, and the total is identifiable BY NAME. The items are `total tractors agriculture` (267 rows), `tractors all purposes` (298), `wheel tractors agriculture` (207) and `crawler tractors agriculture` (180). THE IDENTITY IS PROVEN, NOT INFERRED: across the 177 (label, year-or-period, indicator, unit) groups holding the total and both named parts, total / (wheel + crawler) has median 1.0000 with all three quartiles at 1.0000 and 172 of 177 within 2%. So `total tractors agriculture` IS wheel plus crawler, to the digit. THE FOURTH ITEM IS A SUPERSET, NOT A COMPONENT, AND IT COINCIDES OFTEN ENOUGH TO MISLEAD: `tractors all purposes` includes non-agricultural machines, so it is always >= the agricultural total -- but across the 177 groups holding all four items it is within 2% of that total in 123 (69%), equal wherever a country had no non-agricultural tractors, and larger in 54, up to 4.4x. Alaska 1950 reads total 160 = wheel 150 + crawler 10 while all-purposes reads 700. So this key holds two DIFFERENT correct measures plus the components of one of them, they agree most of the time, and no single value can represent the set. WHAT A CONSUMER PUBLISHES: the WHEP R package collapses duplicate keys with mean(), so a consumer keying on item_code rather than item publishes Alaska 1950 as (10 + 160 + 700 + 150) / 4 = 255.0, which is neither the agricultural total (160), nor the all-purposes figure (700), nor any component. Aden Protectorate 1949 publishes 5.2 against a total of 7.0. THE ITEM AXIS HAS NO AGGREGATE FLAG, which is why this is invisible: `is_aggregate` marks 2,141 fao1952 rows and every one is a GEOGRAPHIC aggregate (ASIA, GENERAL TOTAL, Total central america), so 267 rows of an item literally named `total ...` carry is_aggregate=False and reach matching. `source_detail` names the source file and agrees with `item` exactly (r_fao_inputs_1952_192_194_total_tractors_agriculture.xlsx), so the total is identifiable from two independent columns and flagged by neither. The only other item-level total in fao1952 is `total hard fibers` (4 rows, item_code 103_104, beside abaca, agaves and other hard fibers), and those 4 ARE flagged is_aggregate=True because they sit under GENERAL TOTAL. Related: issue 367 (total-beside-parts and the mean collapse), issue 451.
